about.title: About
about.body:
A personal creative archive

PUNKCANVERSE is Punkcan’s personal site. It collects selected AI video, image and music prompts, credits their original creators, and provides a place for creative breakdowns, technical resources and AI 工作论 essays.

Notes and essays reflect the author’s observations. Original breakdowns and first-hand test notes are published when available; an empty field is not presented as a completed review.

Creators and sources

Prompt copyright belongs to the original creators. Entries link to their authors and source posts. Videos appear through official X embeds. Thumbnails reference public X image URLs directly; we do not host copies of these videos or images.

Find Punkcan on X: @punkcan.

contact.title: Contact
contact.summary: Contact PUNKCANVERSE about attribution, corrections or removal requests.
contact.body:
Get in touch

Email hello@punkcanverse.com or contact @punkcan on X.

Attribution and removal

Creators may use this email to request removal of their work or a correction to a credit or source. Include the page address, the original post and a brief explanation so we can identify the material.

Removal requests may also use the existing takedown page. We aim to process removal requests within 48 hours. You do not need to prove your identity before making a request; we may ask for clarification where necessary to resolve a disputed request.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: How PUNKCANVERSE uses analytics, cookies, embeds and affiliate links.
privacy.body:
Information we use

We use Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to understand visits and improve the site, including pages viewed, basic browser and device information and general location. Reports are used in aggregate. This is not a claim that every event is anonymous: Google receives technical request information, and cookie-based identifiers may be used when you consent. We do not ask analytics to collect your name, email address, private conversations or prompt text.

Cookies and consent

Google Consent Mode v2 defaults analytics storage, advertising storage, advertising user data and advertising personalization to denied. Accepting the banner grants these four categories; rejecting it keeps them denied. We store your choice in localStorage on this browser. The Google tag loads with denied defaults and may send cookieless measurement signals before consent; declining is not a promise that no network request reaches Google.

Change or withdraw your choice

Use the control here or in any page footer. It clears the saved preference, immediately updates all four categories to denied and reopens the banner. You can then reject or make a new choice. Browser settings can clear existing cookies and site storage; changing your choice does not erase information already received by third parties.

Third-party embeds

X embeds load when you choose to play a post. X may set third-party cookies and process request information under its own policies. Thumbnails also load from X image servers. Our Google consent controls do not control X or other third-party websites.

Affiliate links

Some outbound links are affiliate links. Following them may allow the provider or its referral partner to record a referral, use cookies or associate a purchase with this site. See our Affiliate Disclosure and the provider’s own privacy information.

Future advertising

We may introduce Google AdSense advertisements in the future. If enabled, Google and its partners may use cookies or similar technologies to deliver and measure ads, including personalized ads where permitted and based on applicable consent and settings. No AdSense advertising is currently installed. Read how Google uses information from partner sites.

Future newsletter

We may offer an email newsletter through Resend in the future. If you subscribe, your email address would be used to deliver the newsletter and manage the subscription. You would be able to unsubscribe at any time using a link in the email. Newsletter signup is currently hidden; no subscription is created by visiting this site.

Contact and changes

For privacy questions, email hello@punkcanverse.com. We may update this policy when our features or practices change; the date above identifies this version.

terms.title: Terms
terms.summary: Terms for using the PUNKCANVERSE creative archive.
terms.body:
Informational content

This site provides creative references and general information. It is not professional or legal advice. You are responsible for evaluating whether material is suitable for your project and for complying with applicable rules.

Rights and attribution

Prompt copyright and rights in source media remain with the original creators. Providing a source link does not grant a license to reuse that work. Original notes and essays are credited to Punkcan. Videos use official X embeds, and we do not host copies of source videos or thumbnails.

Third-party tools

External services and tools are governed by their own terms, policies and charges. We do not control their availability or content. Links and descriptions do not guarantee results, quality, suitability or continued access.

No guaranteed outcome

AI tools and their outputs can change. Examples and observations are offered without a promise of a particular result. Check the original sources and exercise your own judgment.

Infringement and removal requests

Send a request to hello@punkcanverse.com, identifying the relevant site and source links, your identity or relationship to the work, and what you would like corrected or removed. We review the information and process requests after checking the material; we may ask for clarification. You may submit the initial request without first proving your identity. The takedown page remains available for removal requests.

affiliate-disclosure.title: Affiliate Disclosure
affiliate-disclosure.body:
How referrals work

Some links on PUNKCANVERSE are affiliate or referral links. If you register or purchase through them, this site may receive a commission. You do not pay extra because you used our link.

Clear labels

Affiliate buttons are marked “推广连结” next to the button and use a sponsored link relationship. Where a referral code is available, it is displayed beside the recommendation. A label or link does not guarantee a product’s quality or a result.

Your choice

You can choose whether to follow an affiliate link. The destination provider controls its prices, checkout, tracking and terms. Our Privacy Policy explains the role of referral tracking and third-party cookies.

For questions, contact hello@punkcanverse.com.

tipArticles.fight:
# Writing fight prompts
> These notes combine official guides, creators’ public observations and successes or failures in the archive. The adapted examples below have not been tested.
## One beat at a time
- Build from subject, action, setting, camera and style or light. Split a fight into preparation, contact and reaction.
- Use consecutive timecodes when shots need specific timing. Keep one camera move per shot; state explicitly when you want a single continuous take.
- Put camera language early. Runway uses camera-first descriptions; Hailuo supports bracketed camera cues.
- For Midjourney image-to-video, the original notes use `--motion high`, `--raw` and `--video 1`.
## What the collected examples suggest
| Model | Useful strengths | Watch for |
|---|---|---|
| Seedance | Choreography, multiple shots, long takes | Too many instructions; unclear weapon ownership |
| Kling | Narrative coverage and tension | A punch can be interpreted as another action |
| Hailuo | Speed and energetic motion | Results vary by version |
| Veo | Anatomy and consistent image quality | Restrictive violence checks; action can feel slow |
| Wan | Action examples and longer clips | Complex motion and multiple references need testing |
| Runway | Composition | Materials may render incorrectly |
| Luma | Atmosphere and battlefield light | Fine action details |
| Grok Imagine | Quick short sequences | Keep camera moves simple |
## Common failures
1. Assign each weapon to one character and keep it there throughout.
2. Reduce cuts and use slower continuous action when identities drift.
3. A written single-take request is not a guarantee. Avoid wording that encourages shot changes.
4. Use standard camera terms: a literal crane appeared in one creator’s earlier attempt.
5. Name the strike and its visible result, rather than just asking for a fight.
6. Handheld motion may conceal artifacts, according to a creator’s observations.
7. Try an explicit shutter description when real-time motion is important.
8. Lock clothing and identity with references; trim instructions that do not help.
## Content rules
Check each service’s current policies. Use sparks, dust, sound and reactions instead of injuries; do not use real people’s likenesses without permission. Community suggestions for defeating moderation are not recommended and may breach platform terms.
## Adapted examples — not tested
The following examples are editorial adaptations, not collected test results. Their performance is unknown.


```
Shot 1 [0-4s]: Wide shot, night, a 19th-century Taiwanese farming village with red-brick sanheyuan houses. Two clans face each other across a muddy field, torches raised. Clan A holds bamboo poles and hoes, clan B holds sickles and wooden shields. Firelight flickers on their faces.
Shot 2 [4-9s]: Handheld tracking shot following a young man in a dark cotton tunic as he blocks a sickle with his bamboo pole and sweeps his opponent's legs. Sparks and dust, no blood. Every character keeps the same weapon throughout.
Shot 3 [9-15s]: Slow crane up over the field, a thatched roof catches fire in the background, villagers scatter, smoke rises into the moonlit sky. Cinematic, realistic, 1/500s shutter, historical reenactment.
```

```
Single continuous take, no cuts. A mountain spirit made of mossy stone and glowing ferns rises from a misty forest in central Taiwan and clashes with a giant serpent formed of river water. The camera orbits slowly around them at ground level as their impacts throw spray and leaves into the air. Mythological, stylized, dawn light through the fog, no gore.
```

```
[Tracking shot] Two martial artists in a temple courtyard of an old Taiwanese town. The man in grey blocks a straight punch, counters with an elbow strike, then a spinning sweep kick; his opponent stumbles back and rolls to his feet. Fluid, continuous choreography, real-time speed, no slow motion.
```
tipArticles.wan3:
# Wan 3.0: people, action and emotion
> A summary of official guidance and public creator notes, not a reproduction of the full documentation.
## Structure and timing
[Official Wan 3.0 guide](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/wan3-video-generation-prompt-guide)
- Combine the overall scene, numbered references, timed shots, subject, setting, movement, aesthetics, dialogue, sound, mood and exclusions.
- Keep timestamps continuous. The prompt guide suggests 2–5 seconds per shot; generation documentation suggests 4–6 seconds. Name transitions, or explicitly request a single take.
- Count images, video and audio references separately and refer to them consistently.
- Identify who speaks, quote the line, specify voice reference and lip sync. Use short dialogue.
- Specify slow motion directly; avoid asking for very frequent repeated movements.
- The official optimization command is `/wan3-pe`. Editing and extension requests need clear intent; the notes specify adaptive ratio and duration -1.
## Creator observations
[Ukiyo_il](https://x.com/Ukiyo_il/status/2092548780658708526) recommends one character per reference, a clear opening-to-resolution arc and preparation, contact and result for attacks. [Langby2](https://x.com/Langby2/status/2100161820988440853) found that Seedance prompts did not transfer unchanged. [hii_roto](https://x.com/hii_roto/status/2099495108051951823) found detailed action more helpful than excessive effects. Start at lower resolution to test; fast motion, multiple faces and requested voice language can be unreliable.
## Live-action texture
- Specify the light source, direction and temperature instead of “perfect lighting.”
- Use focal length, depth of field, handheld drift, focus and exposure changes as appropriate.
- Describe skin texture, stray hair and small physical details. Explicitly exclude plastic skin and over-smoothing.
- Write visible reactions rather than emotional adjectives. One core action every 3–5 seconds is easier to follow.
- Lock facial features and clothes separately. Use one character per reference and specify seating or left-right relationships in group scenes.
## Emotion through behavior
The official guidance includes overall mood and a separate style/mood section. Vocal direction combines words, emotion, intonation, speed, timbre and accent. Match blinks, breathing and small head movements to the dialogue; negative instructions can exclude exaggerated blinking or gestures.
[Atlas Cloud’s explanation](https://www.atlascloud.ai/blog/tips/how-to-write-wan-3-0-prompt) recommends a visible action chain rather than an emotion label. A held close-up can show a slow change of gaze or posture.
tipArticles.minimax-h3:
# MiniMax H3 writing notes
> Based on the official Skill and reference material; this is a summary, not the complete documentation.
## Choose the mode first
[Official writing Skill](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/skills/h3-prompt-writing/SKILL.md)
T2VA, I2VA, FL2VA and L2VA use `integrated_multimodal_description`, `overall_soundscape` and `non_diegetic_music`. Ref2VA uses six sections, adding subject definitions, summary, retention analysis and detailed description.
## Build a clear timeline
1. Match the requested duration of 4–15 seconds.
2. Prefer concrete visible and audible details over abstract adjectives.
3. Leave the first shot untimed; later shot timestamps must increase strictly.
4. Describe camera movement by type, amplitude and speed. Medium amplitude and normal speed can be omitted.
5. Keep speaker IDs such as `(S1)` stable. Preserve the original language of dialogue, lyrics and on-screen text.
6. Separate ambient/action/vocal sounds from music that only the audience hears. Use `N/A` when there is no score.
7. Explain how the first or last reference frame joins the timeline.
8. Keep picture, video and audio reference labels consistent throughout.
[Reference details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3/main/skills/h3-prompt-writing/references/base-en.txt)
## Community supplements
[AtlasCloudAI’s collection](https://github.com/AtlasCloudAI/awesome-minimax-h3-prompts) groups reference binding, observable action, spatial relations, camera/editing, visual style, audio and necessary constraints. [BeatAPI’s archive](https://github.com/BeatAPI/awesome-minimax-h3-prompts) provides additional examples. These supplements are not the official Skill text.
